chunks: And he narrated it through another route, from Abū ʿImrān al-Munshid, from Ḥudhayfah ibn Manṣūr, who said:

Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “No, by Allah, the month of Ramadan has not diminished, nor does it ever diminish, from thirty days and thirty nights.” So I said to Ḥudhayfah: “Perhaps he said to you, ‘thirty nights and thirty days,’ as people say, the night comes before the day.” Ḥudhayfah said to me: “This is how I heard it.”

This report is not sound for acting upon for several reasons. One of them is that the text of this report is not found in any of the compiled foundational books; rather, it is only found among anomalous reports. Another is that the book of Ḥudhayfah ibn Manṣūr is free of this hadith, and it is a well-known, famous book; if this report had been authentic from him, he would have included it in his book. Another is that this report has differing wordings and disturbed meanings. Do you not see that Ḥudhayfah at one time narrates it from Muʿādh ibn Kathīr from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, and at another time narrates it from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام without an intermediary, and at another time gives legal opinion by it from himself and does not ascribe it to anyone? This type of discrepancy is among what weakens objection by means of it and reliance upon its like. Another is that even if it were safe from all that we have mentioned, it would still be a solitary report that establishes neither knowledge nor practice, and solitary reports may not be used to object against the apparent meaning of the Qur'an and the mass-transmitted reports that we have mentioned. And even if it were safe from all of that as well, there would still not be in its purport anything requiring acting upon numerical reckoning rather than the crescent sightings. I shall clarify the aspect of that, if Allah wills.

As for the hadith narrated by al-Ḥasan ibn Ḥudhayfah from his father from Muʿādh ibn Kathīr, that he said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “People say that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم fasted twenty-nine more often than he fasted thirty.” He said: “They have lied. The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, from when Allah commissioned him until Allah took him, did not fast less than thirty days, and the month of Ramadan has not diminished, since Allah created the heavens and the earth, from thirty days.” This only indicates the denial of the narrator from the generality concerning the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم that he fasted the month of Ramadan twenty-nine days more often than he fasted it thirty; it does not indicate that fasting it as twenty-nine is invalid, nor that his time necessarily had to be like that. The meaning of “he did not fast, from when he was sent until he was taken, less than thirty days” may be to report what happened for him in that period of time during which Allah made that obligatory upon him, not what might occur in future times after those periods. It is also possible that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم did not fast less than thirty days according to what the opponent claimed in terms of predominance rather than rarity, and prevalence rather than infrequency, as though he said: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم had not fasted less than thirty days in most of his circumstances, according to what the opponents claimed. And his statement, “the month of Ramadan has not diminished, since Allah created the heavens and the earth, from thirty days and thirty nights,” may be understood according to the way the opponents alleged that its diminution from that was more frequent than its completion. So when the speech in this report can bear the meaning we have mentioned, we carry it upon that meaning and reconcile it with the mass-transmitted reports regarding the permissibility of the month of Ramadan being less than thirty days, so that agreement and harmony may occur between the reports from the Truthful Ones عليهم السلام.

As for the hadith of Muḥammad ibn Sinān from Ḥudhayfah ibn Manṣūr from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said, “The month of Ramadan is thirty days; it never diminishes,” and in the other narration, “It does not diminish, by Allah, ever,” this does not establish what the adherents of numerical reckoning have held. That is because his statement عليه السلام, “The month of Ramadan does not diminish ever,” only indicates that it is not always deficient; rather, at times it may be complete and at times deficient. If it were deficient always, it would never be complete in any circumstance, and this is not something held by any of the rational people.

key_terms.أَخْبَارُ الْآحَادِ: solitary reports that do not independently establish certain knowledge or binding practice here
key_terms.الْأَخْبَارِ الْمُتَوَاتِرَةِ: mass-transmitted reports used here as stronger evidence
key_terms.الْأَهِلَّةِ: crescent sightings by which the month is determined
key_terms.الْخَبَرُ: the report or hadith under examination
key_terms.الْعَدَدِ: numerical reckoning for determining the month
key_terms.الْقُرْآنِ: the Qur'an, whose apparent meaning cannot be opposed by solitary reports
key_terms.شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan, the central subject of the report and its legal discussion
key_terms.مَتْنَ: the textual body of the hadith

ai.seo_question: Can the month of Ramadan be less than thirty days according to Shia hadith analysis?
ai.summary: This passage examines reports about whether the month of Ramadan can be less than thirty days and argues that certain narrations used to deny this are not reliable or decisive. It then reconciles those reports with more widely transmitted reports affirming that Ramadan may be either complete or deficient, thus favoring crescent-based determination over fixed numerical reckoning.
